title: Section 119 — Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act

content.overview: BNS s. 119 — Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act. BNS restatement of IPC 327 / 329. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 327 / 329. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 119 is the rule on “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act”. The section provides that (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer, or from any person interested in the sufferer, any property or valuable security, or of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything which is illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 119 exists so that “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
119. (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer, or from any person interested in the sufferer, any property or valuable security, or of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything which is illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

(2) Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for any purpose referred to in sub-section (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt for the purpose of extorting from the sufferer, or from any person interested in the sufferer, any property or valuable security, or of constraining the sufferer or any person interested in such sufferer to do anything which is illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
2. (2) Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for any purpose referred to in sub-section
3. (1), shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

learningObjectives: Master the aggravated offences of extortionate bodily violence under BNS s. 119.
Analyze the specific purposes: extorting property/valuable security, or constraining a person to do an illegal act or facilitate an offence.
Distinguish sub-section (1) (hurt for extortion: up to 10 years and fine) from sub-section (2) (grievous hurt for extortion: life imprisonment or up to 10 years and fine).
Understand the consolidation of IPC ss. 327 and 329.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 119 consolidates extortionate bodily violence: sub-section (1) punishes voluntarily causing hurt for the purpose of extorting property or valuable security, or constraining the sufferer or an interested person to do an illegal act or facilitate an offence, with imprisonment up to ten years and fine; sub-section (2) punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt for any such purpose with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes the weaponization of physical violence and torture used to coerce the transfer of property or compel participation in unlawful activities.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 119 (consolidating IPC ss. 327 and 329).
Sub-section (1): Voluntarily causing hurt for extortion or constraining illegal acts — imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine.
Sub-section (2): Voluntarily causing grievous hurt for extortion or constraining illegal acts — imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
Purposes: (1) Extorting property or valuable security; (2) Constraining sufferer or interested person to do anything illegal; (3) Facilitating the commission of an offence.
essentialIngredients: The accused voluntarily caused hurt (sub-section 1) OR grievous hurt (sub-section 2).
The act was done for the purpose of extorting property or valuable security from the sufferer or any person interested in the sufferer; OR
For the purpose of constraining the sufferer or interested person to do anything illegal, or to facilitate the commission of an offence.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 119 consolidates former IPC 327 and 329 into a single section with two tiers. It targets extortionate violence where physical harm is inflicted as leverage to coerce financial or illegal concessions. The violence may be directed at the property owner or at someone interested in them (such as beating a child to extort money from the father). The purpose must be either extorting property or valuable security, or forcing the victim to perform an illegal act (e.g., forcing a bank manager to falsify records) or facilitate a crime. Because of this predatory coercive purpose, even simple hurt is punished severely with up to ten years imprisonment under sub-section (1), while grievous hurt attracts imprisonment for life under sub-section (2).
examples: Teaching example (Beating to extort ransom/property): Loan sharks kidnap a debtor's brother and repeatedly beat him with clubs to force the debtor to sign over the title deeds of his agricultural land. This constitutes an offence under s. 119(1).

Teaching example (Breaking bones to compel crime): Gang members intentionally break a warehouse watchman's leg to force him to leave the facility gates unlocked for a planned heist. This satisfies s. 119(2) (grievous hurt to facilitate an offence), exposing the offenders to life imprisonment.
distinctions: Section 119 vs Simple Hurt/Grievous Hurt (ss. 115/117): Simple hurt carries 1 year and grievous hurt 7 years; under s. 119, the extortionate/coercive purpose escalates sentences to 10 years and life imprisonment respectively.
Section 119 vs Robbery (s. 307): Robbery involves immediate theft accompanied by violence; Section 119 targets extortionate demands or coercing illegal conduct.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who fractured a businessman's arm while demanding that he transfer equity shares in his corporation to the accused is guilty under s. 119(2).
Rule: Causing grievous hurt for the purpose of extorting valuable security constitutes an offence under BNS s. 119(2).
Application: A bone fracture (grievous hurt under s. 116g) was intentionally inflicted to coerce the transfer of shares (valuable security).
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 119(2) and liable to imprisonment for life.

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 119 consolidation of IPC ss. 327 and 329.
List the twin purposes: extorting property/security, or constraining illegal acts/crimes.
State punishment: hurt (up to 10 years and fine); grievous hurt (life or up to 10 years and fine).

Penalizes causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property or compel illegal acts.
